html:
Essequibo was a Dutch colony on the Essequibo River in what is now Guyana, on the northeast coast of South America. Dutch traders set up the fort of Kyk-Over-Al on an island in the river around 1616.

At first the colony traded with the local peoples for dyes and other goods. Under the Dutch West India Company it turned to sugar, worked by enslaved Africans brought by the Atlantic slave trade. Its long-serving governor Laurens Storm van 's Gravesande opened the nearby Demerara River to settlers, many of them British, in the 1740s.

The Dutch held Essequibo through most of the 1700s, but Britain occupied it during the wars with France and kept it after 1814. In 1831 it was joined with Demerara and Berbice to form British Guiana. Venezuela still claims the land west of the Essequibo River. See also the Dutch Republic and the neighbouring Surinam.
